external.description:
I'm somebody who's written rather extensively on generative AI ethics, and I feel there is a lot that is unethical about the current corporate climate and culture surrounding the technology. And when I write about LLMs and chatbots, I'm careful not to make judgments about the people using the end products—I don't think you're a bad person if you use ChatGPT or Claude, or whatever.

What I'm discussing today is different. There is no room for debate or argument, here—only hard, absolute lines in the sand.

Much of the world has become far too complacent and complicit with people (and their companies) who proclaim and hold far-right, fascist ideology. These are not image boards residing in the fringe corners of an anonymous Internet made up of people who have slipped through the cracks. No, these are wealthy people in power who are blatant and shameless in their support for those who continuously beat the drum of bigotry, xenophobia, transphobia, and cynical accelerationist hatred.

Open source technology has become a culture safe for this rhetoric and ideology, with millions of dollars being invested to continue this status quo.

You need to be made aware of this, and then you need to be vocal and take action.

## DHH

David Heinemeier Hansson is the most well-known figurehead here. He is the creator of Ruby on Rails, CTO of 37signals, and a Shopify board member.

In September 2025, DHH published "As I remember London", mourning that London is "no longer full of native Brits"—a claim that redefines "native Brit" to mean "white." Developer Jake Lazaroff details how DHH describes a Tommy Robinson march as "heartwarming," where speakers called for "remigration" (a euphemism for the ethnic cleansing of non-white residents) and one speaker demanded that countries "ban halal," "ban mosques," and "ban temples." DHH invokes abuse scandals to bolster his white-nationalist rhetoric, framing non-white men as predators of "British girls," while UK data shows no such racial skew. LibreNews reaches the same conclusion.

Developer Joel Drapper wrote how Ruby Central had lost a $250,000-a-year sponsorship from Sidekiq after giving DHH a speaking slot at RailsConf a few weeks later, leaving the nonprofit financially dependent on Shopify (where DHH sits on the board); Shopify then pushed Ruby Central to consolidate control rather than lose its funding. The Register and Heise both covered the fallout.

But none of this has cost DHH money—if anything, he's only gained. A few weeks ago, DHH announced the Omacom Foundation to bankroll his Linux distribution, Omarchy, which is nothing more than a few vibecoded scripts on top of Arch Linux.

There are twelve "Founding Patrons" pledging a million dollars apiece:

  * Tobi Lütke, CEO of Shopify
  * Patrick Collison, CEO of Stripe
  * Michael Dell, Chairman and CEO of Dell Technologies
  * Jack Dorsey, Block Head and Chairman of Block
  * Matthew Prince, CEO of Cloudflare
  * Brendan Iribe, Cofounder of Sesame and Oculus
  * Jason Fried, CEO of 37signals
  * Drew Houston, cofounder and co-CEO of Dropbox
  * Peter Steinberger, creator of OpenClaw
  * Brian Armstrong, CEO of Coinbase
  * Yunjie Dai, cofounder of TapTap
  * DHH himself.



And these corporations are each contributing $100,000 a year for three years:

  * 1Password
  * 37signals



A dozen of the most powerful executives in tech looked at a man who wrote that a British march calling for the deportation of non-white citizens was "heartwarming," and decided he was the person they wanted to hand a multimillion-dollar foundation to.

I should also mention that the same infrastructure companies bankrolling Omarchy and Ladybird are also the backbone of the ongoing violence of U.S. deportations. This includes Amazon's AWS contracts powering ICE, Palantir building ICE's case-management system, and the use of Salesforce's tools.

## "Apolitical"

Andreas Kling, founder of the Ladybird browser project (itself an Omacom-adjacent beneficiary, sponsored by Cloudflare, FUTO, Shopify, 37signals, Proton, and JetBrains), built his project's identity around refusing a documentation patch that would have made SerenityOS's manuals gender-neutral, on the grounds that gender-neutral language was "personal politics" that didn't belong in a technical project. Blogger Kate Vibber wrote how that became Ladybird's official contributing guidelines, which now bar "discussions on societal politics" outright—a policy treating the mere existence of trans contributors as more "political" than excluding them. In 2026, Kling posted in support of Charlie Kirk after Kirk's assassination and, per discussion on Lobsters, bristled at being called a fascist for it—a reaction hard to square with "apolitical," since Kirk was a movement figure who, per his own Wikipedia entry, promoted the "white genocide" conspiracy theory and criticized the Civil Rights Act.

Vaxry, the developer behind the Hyprland Wayland compositor (another Omacom-funded project), was banned in 2024 by Freedesktop.org's Code of Conduct team over a pattern of the Hyprland Discord enabling harassment of trans community members, including an incident where moderators changed a trans user's display name to strip their pronouns. Vaxry's own public response framed the ban as ideological overreach by "social justice warriors," while the Freedesktop side, recounted at LibreNews, describes over a year of private attempts to get him to address the toxicity before going public. Hyprland's contributing guidelines now ban "political" speech too.

Enrico "metux" Weigelt forked the deprecated Xorg server into Xlibre as a rebellion against a "RedHat DEI" conspiracy he believes exists. The founding document of the project was a rant about big-tech diversity initiatives, and its code of conduct is a text file that just says "404." FUTO is a funder of Immich and is run by Eron Wolf, a friend and platformer of Curtis Yarvin, the "dark enlightenment" writer whose ideas about dismantling democracy have now found purchase in the current U.S. administration. Brendan Eich, Mozilla's co-founder and now Brave's CEO, used Brave's infrastructure to give payments to Kiwi Farms, a forum whose harassment campaigns have been linked to multiple suicides.

We witness the same pattern over and over. A tech project is declared "apolitical," and defines any accommodation of marginalized contributors as a political act, and keeps the actual politics of the maintainers—nostalgia for ethnically white homogeneous cities and hostility to gender-neutral pronouns—off the table entirely. Because that's just, you know, how they feel. "Apolitical" has never meant a lack of politics. It's meant politics that current power doesn't have to defend.

## The Throughline

We have been watching the fragile fury of white masculinity and hate metastasize and fester over the years, from Gamergate's harassment campaigns through years of anti-SJW cringe compilation content mills, the marking of Antifa as the enemy, the tantrum-throwing #AllLivesMatter movement, and the manufactured panic over DEI and "wokeism."

You are not living in the neoliberal-Obama era where basic compassion and empathy are the default anymore. And you haven't been for a long time. Despite their cries about censorship and deplatforming, and despite their persecution fetish, these people are not on the fringe. They have board seats and sponsorships and multimillion-dollar foundations.

It is no coincidence this is occuring as companies and brands return to X, as the United States votes at a Midterm election being interfered with by a sitting president, as conservatives normalize the far-right in Europe politics and culture.

If you want a more thorough and longer list of people, companies, and products, then I recommend reading up on Devine Lu Linvega's Fashware list on Sourcehut, as well as Drew DeVault's list of Weird Little Guys.

You may be in a position where the specific harms and rhetoric being spewed are not aimed at you, and you may have been coaxed into viewing what I'm saying here as overreaction, or as a rabid, self-righteous screed. Millions of dollars have been spent to ensure this, and it could not be further from the truth.

We cannot afford to continue to shrug off the presence of these people and their projects in open source. A united stand must be taken.

**Speak up on this**. Boycott aggressively. Let people know you don't support Cloudflare, Shopify, 37signals, Dell, 1Password, Framework, Block, Coinbase, Dropbox, TapTap, and any other company enabling the spread of dangerous and harmful political ideologies that will continue to result in further violence and death. And let people know the harm these companies are actively doing.

We cannot allow this to continue; we must be far more proactive and assertive in our fight against the normalization of fascism and the far right. We must be willing to sacrifice ease and convenience, and we must be willing to sever all connections with these entities.

It is our only way forward.

D’après Apple, la version 27.0 du logiciel des HomePod améliore AirPlay, avec des connexions annoncées comme plus rapides et plus réactives. Une bonne nouvelle, sauf que ces changements ont aussi introduit un bug particulièrement gênant pour une application tierce réputée, Airfoil.

Airfoil. Image Rogue Amoeba.

Rogue Amoeba prévient que tvOS 27 et « HomePod OS 27 » souffrent d’un bug critique empêchant les Apple TV et les HomePod de lire les flux AirPlay envoyés par Airfoil. L’éditeur assure avoir exploré toutes les pistes de son côté avant d’arriver à la conclusion que le problème se situe chez Apple et que seule une mise à jour du système pourra le corriger.

Le dysfonctionnement touche les connexions AirPlay 1, qui ne fonctionnent plus correctement avec les appareils sous les nouvelles versions. Rogue Amoeba ne précise pas si d’autres logiciels sont concernés, mais le problème pourrait logiquement toucher les applications reposant sur le même mécanisme de diffusion.

En attendant une éventuelle correction d’Apple, l’éditeur indique qu’une autre de ses applications audio, SoundSource, continue de fonctionner normalement. Elle utilise en effet un mécanisme de diffusion très différent. SoundSource n’a pas exactement le même rôle qu’Airfoil, car elle sert avant tout de console audio virtuelle pour macOS. Mais comme elle permet aussi de diffuser de l’audio vers des enceintes AirPlay, cela en fait une solution de repli possible.

Les HomePod passent eux aussi à la version 27, avec la fonction AutoMix pour Apple Music
external.title: HomePod OS 27 : Apple améliore AirPlay, mais casse Airfoil au passage

Elon Musk abandonne finalement son bras de fer avec Apple. X Corp et SpaceXAI ont demandé à la justice américaine de mettre fin à leurs poursuites contre Cupertino dans le cadre de leur plainte antitrust visant également OpenAI, rapporte Reuters. Les entreprises du milliardaire ne comptent en revanche pas lâcher l’affaire face au créateur de ChatGPT.

Elon Musk en 2025. Image Gage Skidmore

La plainte remontait à l’année dernière. Musk accusait Apple et OpenAI d’avoir verrouillé à leur avantage les marchés des smartphones et des chatbots d’intelligence artificielle générative, notamment grâce à l’intégration de ChatGPT dans Apple Intelligence. Il reprochait également à Apple de privilégier ChatGPT au détriment de Grok dans l’App Store, notamment dans ses classements et ses sélections éditoriales. Selon lui, ce partenariat désavantageait ainsi des concurrents comme xAI et son chatbot Grok. Musk avait alors attaqué Apple et OpenAI en justice pour entente illégale. Apple avait ensuite demandé le rejet de la plainte, faisant notamment valoir que son accord avec OpenAI n’était pas exclusif.

Elon Musk accuse Apple de privilégier ChatGPT au détriment de Grok et menace de poursuites

On ne sait pas ce qui a poussé les entreprises de Musk à faire machine arrière concernant Apple. Le document déposé devant le tribunal ne précise ni les raisons de l’abandon des poursuites, ni si un accord a été trouvé entre les deux camps. OpenAI veut d’ailleurs en savoir davantage : l’entreprise affirme ne pas avoir participé à l’arrangement entre Apple et les sociétés de Musk et dit en ignorer les modalités.

La situation a quelque chose d’assez ironique, puisque les relations entre Apple et OpenAI sont elles aussi sérieusement écornées. Cupertino a porté plainte contre OpenAI en juillet, l’accusant notamment d’avoir obtenu des secrets industriels par l’intermédiaire d’anciens employés d’Apple partis rejoindre l’entreprise. Depuis, le ton est encore monté, OpenAI qualifiant la procédure d’Apple d’« irréfléchie, agressive et étrangement personnelle ». Le créateur de ChatGPT se retrouve ainsi engagé dans plusieurs contentieux avec des partenaires ou anciens alliés.

X et SpaceXAI maintiennent en effet leurs accusations à son encontre. Cet affrontement avec Elon Musk est loin d’être nouveau : le milliardaire a perdu en mai un autre procès contre l’entreprise qu’il a contribué à fonder, portant notamment sur l’abandon supposé de sa mission d’origine à but non lucratif. Le jury avait alors estimé qu’il avait engagé son action trop tard.
external.title: Elon Musk met fin à son bras de fer avec Apple, mais poursuit OpenAI

C’est devenu une habitude : après le Prime Day de l’été, Amazon organise à l’automne une seconde grande opération commerciale réservée à ses abonnés. Cette année, les « Jours Flash Prime » auront lieu les mardi 6 et mercredi 7 octobre. Le nom change, mais le principe reste le même que pour le Prime Day : pendant deux jours, Amazon proposera une avalanche de promotions accessibles uniquement aux membres Prime.





Le géant du commerce en ligne a d’ores et déjà annoncé la participation de plusieurs marques, parmi lesquelles Bosch, Bose,LG, Lego, Ninja, Oral-B, Philips et Samsung. On s’attend aussi à des remises sur des produits Apple. L’année dernière, l’iPhone 16e, l’iPad A16, le Mac mini ou encore l’Apple Watch Ultra 2 avaient été concernés. L’événement tombe sans doute un peu tôt après la sortie des iPhone 18 Pro et des nouvelles Apple Watch pour espérer de grosses réductions sur ces modèles, mais sait-on jamais.



Pour profiter des offres, il faudra donc être abonné à Amazon Prime. La formule coûte 6,99 €/mois ou 69,90 €/an et comprend notamment la livraison accélérée sur de nombreux articles, ainsi que l’accès à plusieurs services comme Prime Video, Amazon Music Prime ou Amazon Photos. Les étudiants et les 18-24 ans bénéficient toujours d’un tarif réduit de moitié, avec désormais 5 % de cashback automatique sur certains produits du quotidien.



Et si vous ne souhaitez pas vous abonner à Prime, une autre grande période de promotions n’est plus très loin, puisque le Black Friday aura lieu fin novembre. Oui, les réductions ne s’arrêtent quasiment jamais.
external.title: Prime Day : Amazon remet ça les 6 et 7 octobre avec les « Jours Flash Prime »

**Yes, exactly. And this is why I keep coming back to the idea of making this a true Project feature rather than only a shared chat.**

I think there is one additional layer that would make it dramatically more useful:

Each person invited to the Project should be able to bring in selected information from **their own ChatGPT** , not just type into the same conversation.

So Person A could intentionally add relevant conversations, files, images, research, or other context from their ChatGPT account, while Person B could do the same from theirs. Anything outside the Project would remain private unless that person chose to bring it in.

Then the participants could actually call on their respective ChatGPTs during the shared conversation.

For example:

**Person A:** “ChatGPT A, can you recall what we worked out about XYZ and bring that information into this Project so Person B and ChatGPT B can review it?”

Then:

**Person B:** “ChatGPT B, compare that with what we discussed previously and suggest any changes or improvements.”

That is the part I think could make this much more powerful than simply allowing multiple humans to type into one ChatGPT thread.

You would effectively have:

**Person A + their ChatGPT**
**Person B + their ChatGPT**
**Person C + their ChatGPT**
all collaborating inside one shared Project.

The **Project itself becomes the privacy boundary**. Joining the Project would not mean everyone suddenly gains access to everything another person’s ChatGPT knows. Only conversations, files, images, or context intentionally contributed to that Project would become shared.

That could eliminate so much of the current copy/paste problem. Instead of humans acting as messengers between separate ChatGPT conversations, we could simply ask our own ChatGPT to bring the relevant work into the shared space and let everyone, human and AI, build on it together.

That’s really the larger idea I was trying to get at with this concept: not just **multiple humans sharing one ChatGPT conversation** , but **multiple humans and their respective ChatGPTs collaborating inside one shared, persistent Project context.**

I think your description of the problem is spot-on. This is just the extra piece I’d love to see layered on top of it.
external.title: Feature Request: Collaborative Projects With Multiple Users + Their Personal ChatGPTs

I think there is one additional layer that would make it dramatically more useful:

Each person invited to the Project should be able to bring in selected information from their own ChatGPT, not just type into the same conversation.

So Person A could intentionally add relevant conversations, files, images, research, or other context from their ChatGPT account, while Person B could do the same from theirs. Anything outside the Project would remain private unless that person chose to bring it in.

Then the participants could actually call on their respective ChatGPTs during the shared conversation.

For example:

Person A: “ChatGPT A, can you recall what we worked out about XYZ and bring that information into this Project so Person B and ChatGPT B can review it?”

Then:

Person B: “ChatGPT B, compare that with what we discussed previously and suggest any changes or improvements.”

That is the part I think could make this much more powerful than simply allowing multiple humans to type into one ChatGPT thread.

You would effectively have:

Person A + their ChatGPT
Person B + their ChatGPT
Person C + their ChatGPT
all collaborating inside one shared Project.

The Project itself becomes the privacy boundary. Joining the Project would not mean everyone suddenly gains access to everything another person’s ChatGPT knows. Only conversations, files, images, or context intentionally contributed to that Project would become shared.

That could eliminate so much of the current copy/paste problem. Instead of humans acting as messengers between separate ChatGPT conversations, we could simply ask our own ChatGPT to bring the relevant work into the shared space and let everyone, human and AI, build on it together.

That’s really the larger idea I was trying to get at with this concept: not just multiple humans sharing one ChatGPT conversation, but multiple humans and their respective ChatGPTs collaborating inside one shared, persistent Project context.

I think your description of the problem is spot-on. This is just the extra piece I’d love to see layered on top of it.
